units.source_text: 浮舟看到这光景，想道：“此身的厄运果然即将来到！”

en.t: When Ukifune saw this, she thought, "The misfortune of this body is truly about to arrive."

units.source_text: 加之匂亲王来信频问“何日可以相逢”，诉说“缭乱似松苔”的心情，使得她痛苦不堪。

en.t: Moreover, Prince Niou kept sending letters asking when they could meet, pouring out a heart as tangled as moss on a pine, and this made her suffer unbearably.

units.source_text: 她想：“总而言之，我无论追随哪一方面，另一方面必然发生可怕的事情。

en.t: She thought, "In short, whichever side I follow, something terrible is bound to happen on the other side.

units.source_text: 惟有我一身赴死，是最安全的办法。

en.t: The safest course is for me alone to go to my death.

units.source_text: 从前曾有为了两个情夫同样热爱、难于解决而投身入水的事例。

en.t: There was once a case of a woman who was loved equally by two lovers and, unable to resolve it, threw herself into the water.

units.source_text: 我身如果活在世间，定将遭逢痛苦之事。

en.t: If I remain alive in this world, I am certain to encounter painful things.

units.source_text: 则此身一死，又何足惜？

en.t: Then if this body dies, what is there to regret?

units.source_text: 我死之后，母亲当时必然悲伤，但她要照顾许多子女，后来自会忘怀。

en.t: After I die, my mother will surely grieve at first, but since she must care for many children, in time she will naturally forget.

units.source_text: 如果我活在世间，为了行为不端而惹人非笑，忍耻偷生，则母亲悲伤势必更甚。”

en.t: If I live on in this world, become a laughingstock for improper conduct, and go on living in shame, then my mother's grief will surely be even worse."

units.source_text: 浮舟为人天真烂漫，落落大方，而又温和柔顺。

en.t: Ukifune was innocent and openhearted by nature, gracious and unpretentious, and also gentle and compliant.

units.source_text: 但因从小不曾受过高深的教养，缺乏涵养功夫，故一遇困窘，顿萌短见。

en.t: But because she had never received a refined education from childhood and lacked inner discipline, as soon as she met with distress she suddenly conceived a rash, fatal thought.

units.source_text: 她想毁灭旧信，不使后人看见。

en.t: She wanted to destroy the old letters so that no one afterward would see them.

units.source_text: 但并不众目昭彰地一次毁灭，而是逐渐处理，有的就灯火上烧毁，有的投在水里。

en.t: But she did not destroy them all at once in full view of others; instead she disposed of them gradually, burning some in the lamplight and throwing others into the water.

units.source_text: 不悉内情的侍女，以为她即将迁居京中，故把往日寂寞无聊时随意乱涂的字稿毁弃。

en.t: The maidservants, unaware of the real situation, thought she was about to move to the capital, and so was discarding drafts she had idly scribbled in lonely, tedious days past.

units.source_text: 侍从看见了，说道：“小姐何故如此！

en.t: When Jijuu saw this, she said, "My lady, why do such a thing?

units.source_text: 情侣之间真心诚意的通信，不欲让别人看见，尽可藏之箧底，闲时私下取出观看，每一封信各有其情趣。

en.t: Letters exchanged sincerely between lovers, if one does not want others to see them, can simply be hidden at the bottom of a box and taken out privately in idle moments; each letter has its own charm.

units.source_text: 信笺如此讲究，而且满纸都是情深意密、令人感激的言语。

en.t: The paper is so carefully chosen, and every page is filled with deeply affectionate, intimate words that move the heart.

units.source_text: 如此全部毁灭，岂不可惜！”

en.t: Is it not a pity to destroy them all like this?"

units.source_text: 浮舟答道：“有什么可惜！

en.t: Ukifune replied, "What is there to regret?

units.source_text: 这是不可给人看见的。

en.t: These are things that must not be shown to anyone.

units.source_text: 我身在世不长久了。

en.t: I will not remain in this world much longer.

units.source_text: 这些信留在世间，对亲王也是不利的。

en.t: If these letters remain in the world, they will be harmful to the prince as well.

units.source_text: 大将知道了，怪我恬不知耻地保藏这些信，多难为情！”

en.t: If the general learns of them, he will blame me for shamelessly keeping these letters, and how painful that would be."

units.source_text: 她左思右想，不堪悲伤，又犹豫不决起来。

en.t: She thought it over from every side, could not bear her sorrow, and began to waver again.

units.source_text: 因为她也曾隐约记得佛教中有一句话：背亲而死，罪孽最重。

en.t: For she also vaguely remembered a saying in Buddhism: to die in defiance of one's parents is the gravest sin.
